nuggets.text: Bear Bachmeier's unusual No. 47 dates to his youth football days as a running back and middle linebacker.
Bear Bachmeier's animal name traces to a great-grandfather, a deep-voiced fighter pilot who called people 'Tiger.'
Bear Bachmeier became the first true freshman in BYU history to start a season opener, in 2025.
True freshman Legend Glasker scored three touchdowns in the opener: two on catches and one on a jet sweep.
Five different Cougars ran for touchdowns against Utah Tech, a first for BYU in the last 30 seasons.
Kalani Sitake, born in Tonga, is the first Tongan to become a college football head coach.
Kalani Sitake was a three-year starting fullback at BYU under LaVell Edwards, from 1998 to 2000.
Cosmo the Cougar debuted in 1953 in a $73 costume, named for the word 'cosmopolitan.'
Part of North America's largest Jurassic fossil collection was stored under LaVell Edwards Stadium until 2005.
The Cougars have not lost at LaVell Edwards Stadium since November 2024.
